attempts.raw: The geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another. It is a scalar quantity that represents the magnitude of the projection and the cosine of the angle between the vectors. The dot product of two vectors A and B is given by the formula A · B = |A||B|cos(θ), where θ is the angle between the vectors. If A and B are orthogonal, their dot product is zero, and if A and B are parallel, their dot product is equal to the product of their magnitudes. The negative projection of vector A onto vector B is given by -A · B / |B|.

The geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another. It is a scalar quantity that represents the magnitude of the projection and the cosine of the angle between the vectors. The dot product of two vectors A and B is given by the formula A · B = |A||B|cos(θ), where θ is the angle between the vectors. If A and B are orthogonal, their dot product is zero, and if A and B are parallel, their dot product is equal to the product of their magnitudes. The negative projection of vector A onto vector B is given by -A · B / |B|.
